anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly: Concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same objects, producing long blocking chains or deadlocks that stall commit progress. 
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical corruption or logical inconsistency inside data or index pages causes unreliable access-paths and errors during reads or writes. 
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Allocated data, log, or temporary space is exhausted, preventing further page splits, allocations, or log growth. 

When these three root causes coincide, the database experiences a multifaceted failure mode. Applications observe surging lock-wait times and deadlock rollbacks while simultaneously hitting "out of space" or "cannot allocate extent" errors. Corrupted pages or mis-linked index nodes can force the optimizer to abandon efficient index probes and fall back to full scans that touch far more rows, sharply increasing lock footprints, temp-space consumption, and log volume. As space dwindles, auto-extension failures block data-file or log growth, which in turn prolongs open transactions waiting on space, lengthening lock hold times. Corruption-induced retries and recovery attempts inflate transaction counts, amplifying contention, while background integrity checks or rebuilds required to fix corruption compete for the same scarce space and locks. Monitoring shows an interleaving of lock-wait spikes, corruption errors, and space-exhaustion alerts, making it difficult to isolate a single culprit. 

Causally, page or index corruption can trigger unexpected lock escalation or long-running consistency checks that monopolize high-level locks, setting the stage for severe contention. The additional I/O and logging generated by repeated scan retries and rollbacks accelerate space consumption in data, temp, and log areas, pushing the system toward capacity limits. Once space exhaustion occurs, allocation failures prevent lock-holding transactions from completing and releasing resources, further deepening the contention spiral. Conversely, near-full data or log files can impede corruption-repair operations, allowing structural damage to persist and propagate. The feedback loop among locking delays, structural corruption handling, and space shortages culminates in widespread throughput collapse, elevated error rates, and heightened risk of systemic outage.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the timeout in seconds for attempts to acquire metadata locks.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_wait_timeout while attempting to acquire a metadata lock.
entry.workload_impact: The metadata lock acquisition fails and the statement does not proceed.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
